Re: Appeal of denial of hip arthroscopy  
Member: Rowan Novak  
Member ID: W128114844  
Procedure: Hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914  
Reference number: POC-6722E0C945-51497  
Date of denial notice: August 17, 2026

To the Appeals Department:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914. Please conduct a complete reconsideration using the medical records submitted with this appeal and authorize the requested procedure.

The available clinical evidence supports medical necessity:

- I have had 14 months of progressive hip pain that has not improved with rest.
- I completed 24 supervised physical-therapy visits over 14 weeks, from March 27, 2026, through July 3, 2026. Treatment focused on core and hip stabilization and included activity modification. The physical-therapy discharge note documents this course.
- I used NSAIDs for four months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on April 21, 2026, provided only three weeks of partial relief.
- I continue to have sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting. I cannot run or squat.
- Examination documented positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- The June 16, 2026, MRI arthrogram demonstrated an anterosuperior labral tear and cam-type femoroacetabular impingement, with an alpha angle of 68 degrees. The joint space is preserved, and the Tönnis grade is 0.
- There is no active infection or untreated substance use. My BMI is 29, and I am a nonsmoker.

The imaging is clinically meaningful in the context of the symptoms and examination findings. It shows both a structural labral injury and cam-type femoroacetabular impingement. These findings correspond with the sharp anterior groin pain, pain with pivoting and sitting, limited painful range of motion, positive provocative testing, and inability to run or squat. The preserved joint space and Tönnis grade 0 also document the condition of the joint at the time of evaluation.

The records further show that reasonable nonsurgical treatment has been attempted without adequate or durable relief. Physical therapy, activity modification, NSAIDs, and injection treatment have not restored function or controlled the symptoms. The proposed surgery is being requested by Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery, to address the documented structural pathology and persistent functional impairment.

I request that the denial be overturned and that prior authorization for CPT 29914 be approved. If the request is not approved, please provide a detailed written explanation identifying each medical-necessity requirement that was not met and explaining how the submitted imaging failed to satisfy it.

I also request a copy of the exact medical policy and clinical-review criteria applied to this request, including:

1. The policy title and number;
2. The effective or revision date;
3. The complete criteria applicable to CPT 29914;
4. The imaging findings required under those criteria;
5. The clinical-review guideline or criteria version used;
6. The specific records and medical findings relied upon in making the determination; and
7. The clinical rationale for concluding that the June 16, 2026, MRI arthrogram did not support the procedure.

No payer-specific policy governing this denial was identified in the publicly available materials reviewed, so I have not quoted a plan policy in this appeal. Please provide the policy and criteria actually applied to my request so that I can address them fully.

Please associate this appeal with reference number POC-6722E0C945-51497 and confirm receipt. This appeal is being submitted before the February 13, 2027 deadline stated in the denial notice.

Sincerely,

Rowan Novak
